extraction.notes: Read in full (pages 1-12; page 1 is the title only). English report by MDED on the first year (September to December 2023) of the Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030; printed page numbers match the text-file pages. Speaker is MDED as issuing body throughout. Cluster and chapter are empty: the report has no chapter structure and names no accession chapter. Interventions follow the wording: measures listed as carried out in 2023 are adopted or implemented; 'approval of the draft Government decision' (e-KYC, MDocs, e-Democracy) is unclear; activities announced for 2024 are proposed. Left out: background on the strategy's alignment with the SDGs, Digital Compass and National Development Strategy (page 3); the description of the monitoring method and data criteria (pages 5-6); the DEP budget and the 95% contribution exemption (page 5); MDED's publication of digitalisation data on its website (incidental); payment services and electronic money (digital finance, R22) and the IT park extension (IT sector) in the policies table; Government Decision 671/2023 on professional development in cybersecurity and the upskilling plan in lesson 3 (digital skills, not linked to an in-scope recommendation); general closing statements on page 12. The text says 11 indicators were available for reporting, but the table lists 7; all 7 are extracted as metrics. Lesson table cells are read in column order as converted. Doubtful for the analyst: joining and eligibility for the Digital Europe Programme (TECH-DIGI), Law 77/2023 on cross-border parcel deliveries for online commerce. Brain drain (lesson 3) is extracted as a barrier to digital transformation only, not as Chapter 2. No Chapter 2 material. Second-pass check (PC-05) by checker-GOV8d on 5 November 2026: 5 items added (review/RUN-2026-02/second_pass/MDA-GOV-2024-004.csv).

items.stated_text: Also, in 2024, the NDTC will continue its work. In this regard, MDED (acting as the NDTC Secretariat) and the SDU will coordinate and ensure the regular meeting of the NDTC to discuss the progress and problems identified in the implementation of the MDTS.

items.stated_text: As implementation of the MDTS continues, coordination of digital transformation projects and programs with external partners is a priority for the Government. In this respect, the Government of the Republic of Moldova together with its partners will continue the efforts to identify, prioritize and allocate resources efficiently in order to maximize their efficiency in achieving the objectives of the Strategy.
items.summary: Coordinating digital transformation projects with external partners is a Government priority; it will keep prioritising and allocating resources with partners.
